title: Selective preflight tracing hooks and lease-based microbatch sampler for inference hotpath
creator: Ava Chen
description: Reduce tracing overhead on the inference hotpath by introducing a lightweight 'preflight' hook that performs constant-time eligibility checks and a lease-based microbatch sampler that collects candidate spans off-hotpath for deferred decisioning. Goal is to cut per-request tracing CPU and allocation pressure while preserving signal for tail-latency and error analysis.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Preflight hook introduced in ingress proxy with <200ns median CPU impact on hotpath.
2) Lease-based microbatch sampler reduces hotpath allocations by >=40% on P50 traffic and maintains >90% recall on high-latency/error exemplars identified by tail pipeline.
3) No regression on 99th percentile request latency (threshold: <1% relative increase).
4) Rollout controlled via feature flag per deployment tier and observable in grafana dashboard 'obs/tracing/hotpath-sampler'.
implementation_notes:
- Add lightweight deterministic eligibility check: stable hash of route+user_tier+payload_signature, quick denies for low-value routes.
- If eligible, preflight attaches a tiny 8-byte sampler token and a lease TTL to the request context, then returns immediately.
- Sidecar sampler pool consumes tokens at short intervals (lease windows), aggregates spans into microbatches, and performs richer decisioning (heuristics + ML score) off-hotpath.
- Use lease to prevent unbounded queuing; expired leases dropped and counted as sample misses.
- Integrate with existing tail-based pipeline: microbatch output is forwarded to deferred evaluator that can retroactively mark requests for long-term storage.
- Provide metrics: preflight_decisions{allow,deny,invalid}, lease_acquired, lease_expired, microbatch_size, deferred_evals_accepted, sampler_cpu_ns.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: Eliminates most hotpath allocations and complex sampling logic from core inference runtime, preserves ability to capture tails.
- Cons: Adds sidecar complexity and cross-process coordination (leases), small risk of missed exemplars if lease TTLs are misconfigured.
- Chosen compromise: keep preflight extremely conservative (deny-by-default for low-tier routes) and emphasize easy feature-flag rollback.
dev_updates: 2025-01-12 - Ava Chen: Spike completed; microbench harness shows preflight check ~120ns median on c6i-like hardware and <0.5us 99th. Drafted design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Selective+Preflight+Hooks

2025-01-20 - Liam Patel: Prototype sidecar implemented; basic lease grant/renew messaging over unix socket. Initial integration tests passing in dev cluster. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1298

2025-01-28 - Liam Patel: Load test (1k rps mix) shows 42% reduction in tracer-related allocations and 35% lower p50 tracer CPU across inference frontends. Observability metrics added to test grafana: grafana/redwood/obs-hotpath-sampler (internal).
2025-02-02 - QA: Canary started in us-west-2 on 'dev' tier with feature flag; monitoring 99th latency and sampler recall on labelled error datasets.
review_feedback: 2025-01-22 - Maya Rodriguez (PM): Good safety controls. Request adding per-tenant opt-out and a flag to force-emission for red-team test requests.
2025-01-24 - Sofia Anders (SRE): Sidecar adds new subservices to runtime; require health endpoints and per-pod memory caps. Also asked for graceful backpressure semantics when sidecar is overloaded.

2025-01-30 - Rahul Singh (Infra): Suggested switching from leases to token buckets for simpler coordination; we kept leases because token bucket requires centralized state and leases better align with microbatch windows.
comments: 2025-01-15 - Ava Chen: Posting initial perf numbers from spike; need input on default denial policy for trial tenants.
2025-01-21 - Liam Patel: Implemented per-tenant opt-out and admin override endpoints. Documented in design notes.
2025-01-29 - Sofia Anders: Can we add a metric that counts missed-tail-exemplars (heuristic mismatches) so we can observe silent regressions? Added to TODO list.
2025-02-01 - Maya Rodriguez: Approved canary with gating thresholds: sampler recall >=85% on labelled errors or rollback.
risk_mitigation:
- Canary rollout with automatic rollback if 99th latency increases by >1% or sampler recall falls below thresholds.
- Feature flags per-region and per-tenant.
- Instrumentation exposes counters for misses so we can detect silent signal loss quickly.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dev canary (1 app cluster) for 2 days. 2) Region canary in us-west-2 on dev tier for 48h. 3) Gradual ramp to production tiers by tenant size, monitor metrics and error recall. 4) Full rollback path via console feature flag and emergency kill-switch in ingress proxy.
observability_metrics: preflight.allow, preflight.deny, lease.acquired, lease.expired, microbatch.size_histogram, microbatch.batch_cpu_ns, deferred_eval.accepted_count, sampler.miss_detected_count
